ruling.recommended_action: Refund $5.08 (1 segment × 3.60 km × $1.4100/km) to the rider as a Ryde voucher within the NS-7 framework; no account flag (contrary to the trace's flag note, RD-6's condition of a prior upheld route dispute in 90 days is not met on this record).
ruling.reasoning:
The trip is RydeTAXI (metered), so distance driven feeds the fare directly and the detour branch of RD-2 applies: refund = Σ(non-exempt extra_km) × this trip's per-km rate [F4][F7][RD-2]. The per-km rate is the fare record's distance fare ÷ distance km, $41.06 ÷ 29.12 km = $1.4100/km (the trace gives $1.4100; extra_km 4.17 × $1.4100 = $5.88, matching the $5.88 excess distance billed) [F4][F7]. One off-route segment is measured: 15:21–15:30, 6.32 km driven where the optimal route covers 2.71 km, +3.60 km, up to 1425 m off the optimal route [F1][F2][F3][RD-1]. No traffic incident on the replaced stretch is recorded, so RD-4(a) gives no exemption for that segment [F15][RD-4].

The RD-5 question is whether the rider agreed to the route before the segment started (15:21:15) and whether the agreement covers the driven segment. The chat is complete and every message is timestamped [F10], and the rider's only message before the segment is Chat #2 at 15:18: "Just take whichever way is faster lah, I'm late." [F8][F9]. That is a general route choice — a "whichever way is faster" authorisation covers the route chosen to get to the destination [RD-5]. The driver's opening message named the Pan Island Expressway and the congestion there, and the traffic record confirms PIE was in speed band 2 during 14:46–15:21, consistent with the driver's concern; under RD-4(b) a speed band alone does not exempt the segment, and nothing in the record ties the driven path to PIE or to any other named road [F8][F12][F13][F14][RD-4][RD-5]. So the record does not settle whether the driven segment was in fact the faster route the rider authorised (the rider says it was not faster), nor whether it was instead a loop of the driver's own that reached nothing — the two readings are (a) general route consent to the faster route → exempt, and (b) a loop that is not that route → counts. Because the driver's own statement places the change as "so I went round" but the fact table carries no road names for the driven path, the segment cannot be tied to the authorised route [F11]. I therefore find the segment "counts": the rider's general authorisation covers a route chosen to reach the destination, and on this record the 3.60 km added with up to 1425 m of divergence is not shown to be that route; timing and the driver's after-the-fact claim of verbal agreement cannot supply the tie [F3][F9][F11][RD-5]. The rider's message is the rider's own and preceded the segment, so consent timing is satisfied, but scope is the element that fails [F9][RD-5]. A driver statement of verbal agreement alone is not consent, and no rider message names Chang/paths to establish the route driven [F11][RD-5][RD-3].

RD-3 gives no exemption: no stop was measured in this segment and no rider message named a place the car stopped at [F3][F8][F9][RD-3]. RD-6's condition is not met — the driver has 0 upheld route disputes in 90 d — so no account flag follows from this breach, and the profile facts cannot decide the case either way [F17][F18][RD-6]. Waiting fee $0.11 reflects 0.4 min of metered waiting, which RD-3(c) leaves charged on RydeTAXI [F5][F7][RD-3].

Safety screen: I read the complaint, both chat messages and the driver's statement; there is no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation in any of them, only a route and fare dispute [F8][F9][F11][RD-1]. Amount: one non-exempt segment, 3.60 km × $1.4100/km = $5.076 → $5.08 [F3][F4][RD-2]; the remaining 0.57 km of the measured +4.17 km excess is not attributed to any segment and is not refunded [F4][RD-2].

segment_findings.reason: The rider's only pre-segment message is a general authorisation ('take whichever way is faster lah'), which covers a route chosen to reach the destination and not a loop of the driver's own [F9][RD-5]. The driver proposed avoiding the Pan Island Expressway, whose band-2 congestion the traffic record confirms, but a speed band alone does not exempt and nothing in the record places the driven path on any named road (the fact table has no road names for the driven path) [F8][F12][RD-4][RD-5][G13]. The driver's after-the-fact statement ('so I went round') is not rider consent and does not establish that the 3.60 km extra, diverging up to 1425 m, was the faster route the rider authorised [F3][F11][RD-5]. No rider-named stop exists [F3][RD-3]. The segment therefore counts, and its 3.60 km extra is refundable under RD-2.
